title: The Subfield Lattice of GF(pⁿ): the Embedding–Divisibility Criterion

meta.author: Lean Genius
originalContributions: galoisField_embeds_iff_dvd: the embedding criterion GF(p^m) ↪ GF(p^n) (as 𝔽ₚ-algebras) ⟺ m ∣ n, obtained by specializing Mathlib's FiniteField.nonempty_algHom_iff_finrank_dvd to the canonical Galois fields via GaloisField.finrank ([GF(p^k):𝔽ₚ] = k). Mathlib has the abstract finrank-divisibility iff but does not record it for GaloisField p m / GaloisField p n in terms of the exponents m, n.

galoisField_natCard_algHom: counting embeddings — exactly m distinct 𝔽ₚ-algebra homomorphisms GF(p^m) →ₐ GF(p^n) when m ∣ n (from FiniteField.natCard_algHom_of_finrank_dvd specialized to the exponents).
galoisField_natCard_endo: the number of 𝔽ₚ-algebra endomorphisms of GF(p^n) is n (the m = n case; these endomorphisms are exactly the n powers of Frobenius).

exists_subalgebra_finrank_of_dvd / exists_subalgebra_card_of_dvd: every divisor d ∣ n is realised as the degree of a subfield of GF(p^n) — the image of an embedding GF(p^d) ↪ GF(p^n), of degree d and cardinality p^d.

intermediateField_finrank_dvd: conversely the degree over 𝔽ₚ of ANY intermediate field 𝔽ₚ ⊆ K ⊆ GF(p^n) divides n (tower law). Combined with the existence direction this characterizes the subfield degrees of GF(p^n) as EXACTLY the divisors of n — e.g. for GF(2^12) the degrees {1,2,3,4,6,12}.
Concrete instances: GF(2^2) ↪ GF(2^4) but not GF(2^2) ↪ GF(2^3); exactly 2 embeddings GF(2^2) →ₐ GF(2^4); GF(2^12) has a degree-6 subfield but no degree-5 subfield.
prerequisites: Mathlib's GaloisField p n: the canonical Galois field, the splitting field of X^(p^n) − X over ZMod p, with GaloisField.finrank giving [GF(p^n):𝔽ₚ] = n for n ≠ 0
FiniteField.nonempty_algHom_iff_finrank_dvd: for finite-dimensional extensions K, L of a finite field F with L finite, Nonempty (K →ₐ[F] L) ⟺ finrank F K ∣ finrank F L
FiniteField.natCard_algHom_of_finrank_dvd: when finrank F K ∣ finrank F L, the number of F-algebra homs K →ₐ L equals finrank F K
Module.finrank_mul_finrank: the tower law [K:𝔽ₚ]·[GF(p^n):K] = [GF(p^n):𝔽ₚ] for an intermediate field K

mathlibDependencies.description: The engine: an F-algebra homomorphism K →ₐ L between finite-field extensions exists iff finrank F K divides finrank F L. Specialized via GaloisField.finrank it becomes m ∣ n.
When finrank F K ∣ finrank F L, the hom set K →ₐ[F] L has cardinality finrank F K; gives the embedding count m.
[GF(p^n) : ZMod p] = n for n ≠ 0; the bridge turning the abstract finrank-divisibility criterion into the concrete m ∣ n.
An algebra homomorphism out of a field restricts to an isomorphism onto its range; used to transport [GF(p^d):𝔽ₚ] = d onto the image subfield.
The tower law for finite field extensions; gives [K:𝔽ₚ] ∣ n for any intermediate field K of GF(p^n).

overview.historicalContext: The classification of finite fields (the parent entry little-wedderburn-oq-02) says there is exactly one field GF(p^n) of each prime-power order, but tells you nothing about how those fields nest. The subfield structure is the next classical fact, due to the Galois theory of finite fields (Galois, Moore): GF(p^m) sits inside GF(p^n) precisely when m divides n — never otherwise. So GF(2^2) lives inside GF(2^4) and GF(2^6) but not GF(2^3), and the subfields of GF(2^12) are exactly GF(2^d) for d ∈ {1,2,3,4,6,12}, a copy of the divisor lattice of 12. This rigidity is the shadow of a cyclic group: the 𝔽ₚ-automorphisms of GF(p^n) form a cyclic group of order n generated by the Frobenius map x ↦ x^p, and the divisor lattice of subfields mirrors the (upside-down) subgroup lattice of ℤ/nℤ. The subfield lattice is the entry point to the Galois theory of finite fields — the cleanest nontrivial instance of the fundamental theorem of Galois theory, because the Galois group is always cyclic — and underlies coding theory, the factorization of X^(p^n) − X into all monic irreducibles of degree dividing n, and norm/trace theory.
overview.problemStatement: Answer the parent's first open question (little-wedderburn-oq-02-oq-01): formalize the subfield lattice of GF(p^n). Establish the embedding criterion GF(p^m) ↪ GF(p^n) ⟺ m ∣ n as 𝔽ₚ-algebras, count the embeddings (exactly m when m ∣ n, in particular n endomorphisms of GF(p^n)), and characterize the subfield degrees of GF(p^n) as exactly the divisors of n — every divisor d ∣ n is realised by a degree-d subfield, and conversely every intermediate field has degree dividing n.
overview.proofStrategy: The embedding criterion is a specialization: FiniteField.nonempty_algHom_iff_finrank_dvd says Nonempty (K →ₐ[F] L) ⟺ finrank F K ∣ finrank F L for finite-field extensions; rewriting with GaloisField.finrank ([GF(p^k):𝔽ₚ] = k) turns the finrank-divisibility into m ∣ n. The embedding count is the same specialization of FiniteField.natCard_algHom_of_finrank_dvd (= finrank F K = m), with the endomorphism count the diagonal m = n case (dvd_rfl). For the subfield-degree lattice: given d ∣ n, an embedding GF(p^d) ↪ GF(p^n) exists by the criterion, and AlgEquiv.ofInjectiveField identifies its image subalgebra with GF(p^d), so the image has degree d (and cardinality p^d via Module.natCard_eq_pow_finrank); conversely, for any intermediate field K the tower law Module.finrank_mul_finrank gives [K:𝔽ₚ]·[GF(p^n):K] = n, so [K:𝔽ₚ] ∣ n. Concrete instances (GF(2^2) ↪ GF(2^4), no GF(2^2) ↪ GF(2^3), 2 embeddings, a degree-6 but no degree-5 subfield of GF(2^12)) are discharged by norm_num / decide on the divisibility facts.
keyInsights: The whole embedding criterion collapses to three rewrites: nonempty_algHom_iff_finrank_dvd turns 'embeds' into 'finrank divides', and two applications of GaloisField.finrank turn the finrank-divisibility into m ∣ n. The mathematics lives entirely in Mathlib; the contribution is recognizing the specialization and packaging it against the exponents.
A field homomorphism is automatically injective, so 'the hom set is nonempty' already means 'GF(p^m) embeds as a subfield' — no separate injectivity argument is needed.

Subfield degrees of GF(p^n) are EXACTLY the divisors of n: the existence direction (every divisor is realised) uses the embedding criterion plus AlgEquiv.ofInjectiveField to read off the image degree; the converse (every subfield degree divides n) is just the tower law. The two together pin down the degree set without ever counting subfields.

The number of 𝔽ₚ-algebra endomorphisms of GF(p^n) is n — these are exactly the n powers of Frobenius, the cyclic Galois group Gal(GF(p^n)/𝔽ₚ) ≅ ℤ/nℤ developed in the sibling entries. Here it falls out as the diagonal case of the embedding count.

Honest 'mathlib' badge: the deep content (the finrank-divisibility iff, the embedding count, GaloisField.finrank, the tower law) is all Mathlib; the original contribution is the specialization to GaloisField and the subfield-degree characterization, which Mathlib does not record.

sections.title: Concrete Instances
sections.summary: GF(2^2) embeds in GF(2^4) (2 ∣ 4) but not in GF(2^3) (2 ∤ 3); there are exactly 2 embeddings GF(2^2) →ₐ GF(2^4); GF(2^12) has a degree-6 subfield (6 ∣ 12) but no degree-5 subfield (5 ∤ 12).

openQuestions.question: Count the distinct subfields of GF(p^n) as the number of divisors of n, by promoting the subfield-degree characterization to a bijection: show the degree map from intermediate fields to divisors of n is a bijection (uniqueness of the subfield of each degree), e.g. via the Galois correspondence with the cyclic group ℤ/nℤ and its one-subgroup-per-divisor structure.

crossReferences.description: The parent classifies finite fields up to isomorphism (one field GF(q) per prime power q). This entry answers its first open question by establishing how those fields nest: the embedding criterion GF(p^m) ↪ GF(p^n) ⟺ m ∣ n and the subfield-degree lattice.

Develops the cyclic Frobenius–Galois group Gal(GF(p^n)/𝔽ₚ) ≅ ℤ/nℤ of order exactly n. The endomorphism count n here is the order of that group; the embedding criterion complements the automorphism story rather than re-proving it.

conclusion.summary: The subfield lattice of GF(p^n) is established as the parent classification's first open question. The embedding criterion GF(p^m) ↪ GF(p^n) ⟺ m ∣ n is obtained by specializing Mathlib's finrank-divisibility iff (FiniteField.nonempty_algHom_iff_finrank_dvd) through GaloisField.finrank. The number of 𝔽ₚ-algebra embeddings GF(p^m) →ₐ GF(p^n) is exactly m when m ∣ n, and the number of endomorphisms of GF(p^n) is n. The subfield degrees of GF(p^n) are characterized as exactly the divisors of n: every divisor d ∣ n is realised by a degree-d (order-p^d) subfield, and every intermediate field has degree dividing n by the tower law. Concrete instances confirm GF(2^2) ↪ GF(2^4) but not GF(2^3), exactly 2 embeddings GF(2^2) →ₐ GF(2^4), and a degree-6 but no degree-5 subfield of GF(2^12). 133 lines, 6 theorems, 0 definitions, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.
conclusion.implications: The engine — the finrank-divisibility iff, the embedding count, GaloisField.finrank, and the tower law — is Mathlib's (hence the mathlib badge); the original content is the specialization to the canonical Galois fields and the subfield-degree characterization, which Mathlib does not record. This makes the gallery's finite-field material structurally usable: not just which finite fields exist, but how they nest, indexed by the divisor lattice.
openQuestions: Promote the subfield-degree characterization to a count of distinct subfields = number of divisors of n, via uniqueness of the subfield of each degree (Galois correspondence with cyclic ℤ/nℤ).
Combine with little-wedderburn-oq-02-oq-02 (monic-irreducible count) to factor X^(p^n) − X over 𝔽ₚ into all monic irreducibles of degree dividing n.
